formative_worksheets.title: Mid-Unit Place-Value Check-In
formative_worksheets.when_to_use: After Lesson 3, before Lesson 4. A 10-minute mid-unit check confirming B1.1 (place value), B1.2 (compare), and B1.5 (even/odd) before Day 4 introduces estimation.
formative_worksheets.purpose: Standalone formative assessment. Lets the teacher see which children can read three-digit numbers fluently, decompose flexibly, compare with place-value reasoning, and apply the last-digit rule before estimation work.
formative_worksheets.student_learning_goal: I can read, decompose, compare, and tell even or odd for any number to 200.

header.student_learning_goal_banner: I can read, decompose, compare, and tell even or odd for any number to 200.
header.character_watermark: Hugo, Tina, and Ona together in the top-right corner. Small (~1.5in tall combined).

prompts.prompt: Three numbers, three jobs. For each: write a decomposition, compare to the next number, and tell even or odd.
prompts.visual_layout: Top half. Three rows. Each row: a target number, a decomposition slot, a comparison slot (with a second number and < / > bubbles), and an EVEN / ODD bubble.

image_placeholders.description: Three rows in B&W line-art, stacked. Each row ~7in × 1.4in. Pre-fills: Row 1 — number 134, decomposition slot, comparison '134 vs 143', even/odd bubble. Row 2 — number 89, decomposition slot, comparison '89 vs 102', even/odd bubble. Row 3 — number 175, decomposition slot, comparison '175 vs 178', even/odd bubble.
image_placeholders.placement: Top half of the page; full-width.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image FORM_Q1_THREE_ROWS: keywords (decomposition, compare, even-odd) name what the rows show.

prompts.prompt: Order these five numbers from smallest to biggest: 67, 134, 89, 178, 145.
prompts.visual_layout: Middle. Five number cards on the left and five empty boxes with right-arrows on the right.

image_placeholders.description: An ordering layout in B&W line-art, ~7in × 2.5in. Five number cards (67, 134, 89, 178, 145) on the left in random order. Five empty boxes in a row on the right with right-arrows between them.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image FORM_Q2_ORDER_FIVE: keywords (order, smallest, biggest) name what the layout asks for.

prompts.prompt: How are you feeling about Place Value Detective work? Circle the face.
prompts.visual_layout: Bottom of the page. Three faces in a horizontal row. Below each: 'GOT IT!', 'ALMOST!', 'TRY AGAIN!'.

image_placeholders.description: Three round face icons in a row, each ~1.5in across. Smile, neutral, frown. Below each, the labels.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image FORM_Q3_FACES: keywords (got, almost, try) name the labels.

prompts.answer_key: Open. Compare with prompts 1 and 2 results.

formative_worksheets.teacher_notes: Administer between Lesson 3 and Lesson 4. Print one per child. Score guide: 3/3 row tasks correct + ordering correct + confident self-rating = ready for Lesson 4. 2/3 row tasks + correct ordering = brief 1:1 conference. <2 row tasks correct = small-group reteach using base-ten blocks before Lesson 4.

reflection_sheet.title: My Place Value Detective Reflection
reflection_sheet.purpose: End-of-unit metacognition. Children look back at their week of place-value work, rate themselves, name a favourite manipulative, name a struggle, set a forward goal.
reflection_sheet.student_learning_goal: I can think about what I learned this week.

header.student_learning_goal_banner: I can think about what I learned this week.
header.character_watermark: Hugo holding a Junior Place Value Detective certificate in the top-right corner. Small (~1.5in tall).

reflection_sheet.teacher_notes: Hand out at the very end of Lesson 5. Allow children to take home as a self-assessment artifact. Compare each child's reflection with their summative score: high reflection + high summative = ready for next unit; mismatches signal confidence-building or remediation needs.
